name: clock
title: Clock face
tagline: Analogue clock with hands placed faithfully from a time (3:30 is mid-way); derived angle arc between two arms in degrees or as a fraction of a turn.
description: An analogue clock face with an hour hand and a minute hand placed from a stated time, hour and minute ticks, and the 1–12 numerals. The hand positions are computed from the time — the hour hand moves 30° per hour plus 0.5° per minute, the minute hand 6° per minute — so the figure is always faithful (at 3:30 the hour hand sits half-way between 3 and 4, not on the 3). An optional angle arc marks the angle between two arms — the hour hand, the minute hand, or the 12 o'clock reference — and its size is derived: the minor angle by default, the reflex (major) angle on request, read out in degrees and/or as a fraction of a turn (75° = 5/24 of a turn, 90° = 1/4). The digital time can be shown or occluded for telling-the-time questions, and the angle value occluded for "find the angle" questions. The marked angle is drawn in amber (the result); the hands are accent-blue content told apart by length and weight.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a clock face is the figure: the angle between the hands at a given time, telling the time, and fractions / multiples of a turn. Author the time as { hour, minute } (hour 0–23, taken mod 12 for the dial; minute 0–59) — every hand position and angle is computed from it, you never place a hand. Angle between the hands: add angle: { from: "hour", to: "minute" } to mark and measure it — this is the case to teach carefully, because the hour hand drifts (at 3:30 the angle is 75°, not 90°; at 3:00 it is exactly 90° — show both). angle.show chooses the readout: "degrees" (default) labels the arc "75°", "fraction" labels it as a fraction of a turn, "both" shows "75° = 5/24 of a turn", "none" draws the wedge with no value (a measure-it answer space). angle.reflex: true marks the major (reflex) angle instead — use it for three-quarter / 270° turns. angle.occlude renders the value as "?" for a "find the angle" question. Fractions / multiples of a turn: set the time so a hand lands on the target (12:15 puts the minute hand on the 3) and mark angle: { from: "twelve", to: "minute", show: "both" } to read "90° = 1/4 of a turn"; hide the hour hand with show: { hourHand: false } for a clean single-pointer turn; the 12 o'clock arm is drawn as a dashed reference ray. Telling the time: leave the angle off; digital: { show: true } reveals "3:30" beneath, digital: { show: true, occlude: true } shows "?" so pupils read the hands and state the time. Furniture: show.minuteTicks false leaves only the 12 hour ticks (a simpler KS2 dial); show.numerals false bares the dial for a turn demo. Keep the same time-of-day framing and the same show settings across a lesson so pupils track one clock. Synonyms a teacher might use: clock, clock face, analogue clock, telling the time, o'clock, half past, quarter past / to, angle between the hands, angle on a clock, turn, full turn, quarter turn, half turn, fraction of a turn, right angle, reflex angle, degrees.

time.description: The time the hands show. Both hand positions are computed from it — you never place a hand. The hour hand drifts with the minutes (30° per hour PLUS 0.5° per minute), so half past three really does sit the hour hand half-way to four.

hour.description: The hour, 0–23 (taken mod 12 for the dial, so 15 and 3 draw identically; 0 and 12 both show 12 on the digital readout).

angle.description: Mark and measure the angle between two arms. Omit this for a plain clock (telling the time, or an answer space with no angle). The arc is drawn in amber (the result); its size is computed from the arms — you never write an angle value.

from.description: One arm of the angle: the "hour" hand, the "minute" hand, or "twelve" (the 12 o'clock reference, drawn as a dashed construction ray). Default "hour".

to.description: The other arm — "hour", "minute" or "twelve". Default "minute" (so the default angle is hour-hand to minute-hand). Must differ from "from".

reflex.description: Mark the REFLEX (major) angle — the long way round — instead of the minor angle. Use for three-quarter / 270° turns and reflex-angle questions. Default false (the minor angle, ≤ 180°).

show.description: "degrees" (default) labels the arc with the angle in degrees ("75°"); "fraction" reads it as a fraction of a turn beneath the clock ("5/24 of a turn"); "both" shows degrees on the arc AND "75° = 5/24 of a turn" beneath; "none" draws the wedge with no value (a measure-it answer space).

occlude.description: Render the angle value as "?" — the "find the angle" hook. The arc still shows; only the number hides. Default false.

digital.description: The digital time readout beneath the clock (e.g. "3:30"). Omit for none.

show.description: Show the digital time beneath the clock. Default false (the hands alone are the figure).

occlude.description: Render the digital time as "?" — the telling-the-time hook ("read the hands; what time is it?"). Implies the readout is shown. Default false.

numerals.description: Show the 1–12 numerals around the dial. Default true. False bares the dial (a turn demo).

minuteTicks.description: Show the 60 minute ticks. Default true. False leaves only the 12 hour ticks (a simpler dial).

hourHand.description: Draw the hour hand. Default true. False for a single-pointer (minute-hand) turn demo.

minuteHand.description: Draw the minute hand. Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the clock; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the clock, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
